road.name: Foss River Road (FR 68) and West Fork Foss Road (FR 6835)
road.status: Open seasonally; the upper section has experienced road damage limiting access, and weekday construction delays (~30 min) are posted May-September
road.driveNote: From Skykomish, follow US-2 east about 2 miles to Foss River Road (FR 68), then continue about 4.7 miles and turn left onto FR 6835 (West Fork Foss Road); park on its shoulder about half a mile on, just after the concrete bridge over the East Fork Foss River. Expect ~30-minute delays for road construction May–September on weekdays 6am–8pm (per USFS alert).

access.fees: $10 per person backcountry recreation fee (mid-May through early October) plus $6 reservation fee
access.notes: 60% of sites (Boston Basin/Eldorado/Sulphide Glacier/etc.) are reservable in advance via Recreation.gov (2026 lottery Mar 2–13); the remaining 40% are walk-up, obtained in person the day before at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.
access.rules: Group size capped at 6 in off-trail cross-country zones (12 in on-trail corridors). Boston Basin camping restricted to two designated sites (Low Camp ~5,300 ft, High Camp ~6,400 ft). Bear canisters required in some zones — free loaners at permit offices.

road.name: Foss River Road (FR 68)
road.status: Gravel, rough with potholes; passable to most passenger cars but high-clearance/AWD recommended
road.driveNote: 4.1–4.2 mi from US 2 (0.5 mi east of the Skykomish Ranger Station) to the East Fork Foss River/Necklace Valley trailhead (~1,600–1,650 ft); the last mile can hold snow into early summer.
road.seasonalGate: No seasonal gate, but intermittent daytime closures/delays are posted for FR 68 from mid-July through fall 2026 for powerline trenching — check the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF alerts page before driving up.

access.fees: $10 per person plus a $6 nonrefundable permit fee, charged mid-May through early October; no charge the rest of the year; free for youth 15 and under.
access.notes: No trailhead or parking fee - the Thunder Creek Trailhead at Colonial Creek begins on National Park Service land, where no Northwest Forest Pass is required. No specific climbing permit.
access.rules: Group size capped at 6 in off-trail cross-country zones (12 in on-trail corridors). Boston Basin camping restricted to two designated sites (Low Camp ~5,300 ft, High Camp ~6,400 ft). Bear canisters required in some zones — free loaners at permit offices.
access.permit: NPS wilderness/backcountry permit required for all overnight stays. Reserve in advance on recreation.gov (roughly 15% odds in the 2025 early-access lottery) or get a walk-up permit in person (about 40% of sites are walk-up only) up to 24 hours ahead at the Wilderness Information Center, 7280 Ranger Station Rd, Marblemount, WA (SR 20 milepost 105.3).
access.closures: None — Colonial Creek/Thunder Creek trailhead is west of SR 20's winter closure gates (MP134-171) and is generally reachable by car year-round, independent of the climbing season.

access.closures: Easy Pass Trailhead (primary approach, SR 20 MP151) sits INSIDE SR 20's winter closure zone (gates at MP134-171) and is unreachable roughly December through mid-spring; exact open/close dates vary year to year (2026 reopened unusually late, June 14, due to storm-repair work) — check WSDOT before a trip. The alternate Thunder Creek/Colonial Creek Campground trailhead (~SR 20 MP130) sits outside the closure gates and is open year-round, but is a longer approach (~13 mi one-way vs. Easy Pass's ~10 mi one-way to the lake camp).

access.fees: Backcountry camping fee is $10/person plus a one-time $6 non-refundable reservation fee, charged mid-May through early October; no charge outside that window and none for youth 15 and under. There is no park entrance fee for North Cascades NP.
access.notes: 60% of sites (Boston Basin/Eldorado/Sulphide Glacier/etc.) are reservable in advance via Recreation.gov (2026 lottery Mar 2–13); the remaining 40% are walk-up, obtained in person the day before at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.
access.rules: Group size capped at 6 in off-trail cross-country zones (12 in on-trail corridors). Boston Basin camping restricted to two designated sites (Low Camp ~5,300 ft, High Camp ~6,400 ft). Bear canisters required in some zones — free loaners at permit offices.
access.permit: A backcountry permit is required for any overnight stay in the park; get it at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount ((360) 854-7245) or the Golden West Visitor Center in Stehekin. About 60% of sites are reservable in advance on Recreation.gov; the remaining ~40% are walk-up only, issued in person up to 24 hours ahead.
access.closures: Camping is prohibited at Park Creek Pass itself to protect fragile alpine turf — plan to camp at Thunder Basin, Park Creek, or the high basin instead. Trail washouts have periodically hit the Bridge Creek/North Fork corridor near Stehekin, sometimes requiring a bike-and-hike detour around damaged sections — check current NPS trail conditions before relying on that approach. A major December 2025 atmospheric-river flood also severely damaged Stehekin's Company Creek Road, power, and wastewater infrastructure, disrupting North Cascades Lodge services and the Stehekin shuttle/ferry into the 2026 season; an interim road repair was completed in June 2026 but services remain limited — check the NPS Stehekin Flood Response Update page before planning the Stehekin/Park Creek approach.
access.seasonal: Cascade River Road (the access road for these trailheads) has a history of washouts/closures — check current NPS road-conditions page each season.
